simple.meaning: אֵיפָה (ʼêyphâh) appears 40 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced in connection with priesthood. The occurrence trail connects the name with an offering.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Judges, and 8 more, beginning at Exodus 16:36. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as offering, altar, priesthood, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֵיפָה (H374) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows אֵיפָה through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.

definitions.short: an ephah or measure for grain; hence, a measure in general
definitions.full: H374. ephah אֵיפָה 35 , אֵפָה noun feminine ephah (etymology dubious, ᵐ5 . οιφι etc., compare Coptic ôipi , Thes Lag Or. ii. 2 & cit .) — ׳א Num 5:15 +; אֵפָה Exod 16:36 +; construct אֵיפַת Lev 19:36 +; — ephah , a grain-measure. 1 a certain quantity of wheat, barley , etc. = ten omers ( עֹמֶר ) Exod 16:36 (compare in measure of offerings Lev 5:11 ; 6:13 ; Num 5:15 ; 28:5 , all הָא ׳עֲשִׂירִית ; = 1/10 chomer ( חֹמֶר ) Ezek 45:11 (= bath, בַּת , liquid measure q. v.) compare Isa 5:10 ; chiefly of offerings, see above & 1Sam 1:24 ; Ezek 45:13 (twice in verse); 45:24 (3 t. in verse); 46:5 (twice in verse); 46:7 (3 t. in verse); 46:11 (3 t. in verse); 46:14 ; compare Judg 6:19 , but also of food 1Sam 17:17 compare Ruth 2:17 & Isa 5:10 above 2 receptacle or measure, holding an ephah , in prophetic vision Zech 5:6-7 , 8 , 9 , 10 ; just measure אֵיפַתצֶֿדֶק Lev 19:36 (|| צ ׳הִֶין ׳אַבְנֵיצֿ, ׳מאֹזְנֵיצֿ, ) compare Ezek 45:10-11 , וָצ ׳שׁלֵמָה אֵיפָה Deut 25:15 (|| שׁ ׳אֶבֶן ׳וָצ ); of unjust measure וְאֵיפָה אֵיפָה 25:14 ; Prov 20:10 ; א ׳הַקְטִין Amos 8:5 ; רָווֺן אֵיפַת Micah 6:10 . (On the actual size of ephah, compare בַּת ). אֵיפֹה see below אַי . P.33 אושׁ אישׁ, (Stem assumed in Thes for אִישׁ ; existence & meaning somewhat dubious Thes (Add) & most derive אִישׁ from [ אִנְשְׁ ] √ אנשׁ (q. v.) In favour are plural אֲנָשִׁים , feminine אִשָּׁה = [ אִנְשָׁה ], lack of proven √ אישׁ , & lack of clear parallels for אישׁ in cognate languages. Against the derivation of אִישׁ from inš is the vocalization ( ִ י , and that fully written, not ֵ ), maintained even with suffixes, the (rare) plural אִישִׁים , the impossibility of deriving אִישׁ & אִשָּׁה from same √ ( אִשָּׁה from ), the existence of אֱנוֺשׁ as parallel form, and the (exceptional) parallel Aramaic איש (Inscription of Carpentras), also Arabic (compare Frey) || ; MI, SI, Phoenician אש are not decisive; Sabean has both אסם & אנסם ; the former apparently = אִישׁ , the latter אֱנוֺשׁ ; but on former compare DHM ZK 1884, 360 & SabDenkm 37. On the whole, probability seems to favour √ אישׁ ; Thes gave meaning be strong ; Dl HA 9, Pr 161 compare Assyrian išanu , strong (compare Dl w. p. 244 ), & proper name יְהוֺאָשׁ ; compare also Prät LOPh Feb. 1884 ; otherwise DHM l. e. & ZMG 1883, 330 & especially Nö ZMG 1886, 739 Lag BN 68 ; compare also Wetzst in De Psalmen, ed. 4, p. 888 and others see also אֱנוֺשׁ אנשׁ, ).
